question: What happens when you take in more food energy (calories) than your body burns off?

options.A: Excess energy is stored primarily as fat
options.B: The body uses up its protein stores completely
options.D: Metabolic rate drops permanently to zero

explanation: Think of it like money: if you earn more than you spend, you save the extra! The body packs away extra calories as fat tissue to use for a rainy day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h1)

question: Why is keeping a good energy balance important for your patients?

options.A: It keeps body weight and energy stores stable
options.B: It ensures the digestive tract never has to rest
options.C: It stops all cellular chemical reactions
options.D: It prevents the need for any physical activity

explanation: Energy balance just means calories in equal calories out. It is what stops a patient from experiencing sudden, unwanted weight changes. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h1)

question: To get an accurate Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) measurement, what condition is needed?

options.A: A complete overnight fast of at least 12 hours
options.B: A warm environment with high physical activity
options.C: Immediate completion of a heavy physical workout
options.D: Consumption of a high-protein meal just before testing

explanation: To see what your body burns at absolute rest, we need digestion and recent activity completely out of the picture. An overnight fast does the trick! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h2)

question: Why is a patient's Resting Metabolic Rate (RMR) usually a bit higher than their BMR?

options.A: It allows for less strict measurement conditions and recent rest
options.B: It includes the energy burned during heavy weight lifting
options.C: It requires the patient to be completely unconscious
options.D: It is measured only during intense aerobic exercise

explanation: RMR is measured when the patient is relaxed, but not under the super strict laboratory rules of BMR. Little movements or recent digestion can bump the numbers up slightly. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h2)

question: Which hormone acts like the body's main thermostat for controlling metabolism?
explanation: Thyroxine, made by the thyroid gland, sets the speed at which your cells turn nutrients into energy and heat. Great hormone to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h3)

question: A patient comes in with a severe infection and a high fever. What should the nurse expect to happen to their metabolic rate?

options.D: Metabolic rate fluctuates only during sleep

explanation: Fever acts like stepping on the gas pedal for your cells! Chemical reactions speed up, which is why febrile patients burn through energy so fast. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h3)

question: What does the term 'Thermic Effect of Food' actually mean?

options.A: The heat lost through the skin after eating spicy food
options.B: The energy stored as fat immediately following digestion
options.C: The drop in body temperature right after a heavy meal
options.D: The energy used to digest and process consumed nutrients

explanation: Even eating takes work! Your body burns calories just chewing, digesting, and processing what you swallow. That is the thermic effect. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h4)

question: Which type of nutrient requires the most energy for the body to break down and process?
explanation: Protein is tough work for the gut! It takes way more metabolic effort to process protein than it does for fats or simple carbs. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h4)

question: What does indirect calorimetry measure to figure out a patient's energy use?

options.A: Total body fat percentage using electrical currents
options.B: Blood glucose levels over a twenty-four hour period
options.C: Oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production
options.D: Internal core body temperature via skin sensors

explanation: By checking the air a patient breathes in and out, this clever test calculates exactly how much energy their cells are burning. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h5)

question: Why can predictive formulas (like the Harris-Benedict equation) sometimes be misleading for critically ill patients?

options.A: They measure direct body heat rather than gas exchange
options.B: They require the patient to be placed inside a sealed heat chamber
options.C: They only provide estimates and may miscalculate actual needs during severe illness
options.D: They can only be used on healthy newborn infants

explanation: Formulas use averages for healthy people. But when a patient has severe burns or trauma, their body behaves unpredictably, so formulas can miss the mark. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h5)

question: What kind of metabolic shift is typically triggered by major trauma, severe burns, or sepsis?
explanation: 'Hyper' means high! Severe physical stress forces the body into overdrive to fight off infection and heal wounds quickly. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h6)

question: Why does the body slow down its metabolism during long periods of starvation?

options.A: To conserve remaining energy stores and prolong survival
options.B: To build up extra muscle tissue in the limbs
options.C: To prepare the digestive tract for a heavy meal
options.D: To increase physical activity levels automatically

explanation: It is a brilliant survival mechanism. When food is scarce, the body dials down its energy use so it doesn't burn through its fat and muscle too fast. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h6)

question: Which nursing action is best for keeping track of a patient's ongoing nutrition?

options.B: Measuring indirect calorimetry on every single shift
options.C: Calculating precise basal metabolic rate without a formula
options.D: Recording daily weights and monitoring food intake

explanation: Never underestimate the basics! Daily weight checks and watching how much food actually gets eaten give nurses the best clues on nutritional health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h7)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient recovering from major surgery. Who is the best healthcare professional to consult for a custom diet plan?
explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Dietitians are the absolute experts at calculating precise calories and nutrients for patients who need special nutritional healing. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h7)
